chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from one of his men, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said:

The penalty is indeed doubled for what is less than the Bidadah (a specific type of camel), until it reaches the Bidadah. So when it reaches the Bidadah, it is not doubled, because it is the greatest that can be.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And whoever magnifies the rituals of Allah, then indeed it is from the piety of the hearts.'

key_terms.الْبَدَنَة: A mature female camel, used here as a standard unit of measurement for animal size in legal penalties
key_terms.شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ: The rituals or symbols of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the rule for doubling the penalty for hunted game in Ihram based on the size of the animal?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi outlines the graduated structure of damm (expiation) for hunting in the Haram, establishing the Bidadah (a mature female camel) as the capstone of the penalty scale to prevent excessive burden. Scholarly tradition interprets the cessation of multiplication at this point as a recognition of the Bidadah's status as the 'greatest' standard unit, reflecting divine mercy in legal proportionality. The concluding verse, 22:32, is contextualized here not just as a general principle of piety, but specifically linking the ritual precision of the Haram's boundaries and sacrifices to the internal state of the believer's heart.
